senses: Finely chopped mince as used in South Asia cookery, typically lamb with peas or potatoes and spices, sometimes used as a filling in samosas or naan.
ety: From Urdu قیمہ, from Persian قیمه (qime), from Turkic, perhaps Ottoman Turkish قیمه (kıyma), whence Turkish kıyma. Doublet of gheimeh, an Iranian meat stew.

senses: Referring to minky fabric.
The fleshy red crest of a rooster.
A red cap once worn by court jesters.
A yellow rattle, Rhinanthus minor (flowering plant native to Eurasia).
An annual garden plant (Celosia argentea var. cristata, syn. Celosia cristata), having showy red clusters of flowers.
ety: From Middle English cokkes comb; equivalent to cock + -s- + comb.

senses: A stupid or clumsy person.
A coastal rockfish of California, Sebastes chlorostictus.
Designed or intended to combat or eliminate spyware on a computer system
examples: Ms. Amero and her supporters said the computer lacked a firewall or antispyware protections to prevent inappropriate pop-ups.

senses: A Japanese middle-aged woman.
A Japanese aunt.
examples: The boys resist the Japanese names by which the obasans of the camp address them as willfully as they renounce any identification with the fragmented body of the aged grandfather.

Elderly gents in berets walked past us, elegant with walking canes, escorting obasans, grandmothers in gleaming tabi socks and geta clogs, treading lightly upon the path with a fixedness approaching solemnity.
Obasans. Every block in Tokyo has one such lady who sees that everyone on the block packages their garbage correctly.

senses: Able to be examined.
Eligible to appear in an examination.
examples: Revise all of the examinable material.

senses: The inner layer of the skin.
ety: Learned borrowing from New Latin derma, from Ancient Greek δέρμα (dérma, “skin, hide”). Doublet of derm.

senses: One who quells; one who overpowers or subdues.
ety: From Middle English queller, quellere, quellare, from Old English cwellere; equivalent to quell + -er.

senses: A blackcurrant plant (Ribes nigrum); the flavor of its berries.
A liqueur made from these berries, especially crème de cassis.
A wine flavor note, suggesting the fruity and full-bodied characteristics of the fruit; mostly referred to as simply blackcurrant in the UK, where the fruit is common.
ety: Borrowed from French cassis (“black currant”), probably from Latin cassia, from Hebrew קציעה (qetzi'ah).
examples: Cassis and soda is a popular drink.
The bartender looked at her malevolently for a moment, shook his head, and walked away to mix the drink. "I never had one of those, those vermouth cassises," Freddie said.

senses: A thick Italian pasta sauce, made with guanciale, grated cheese, beaten egg yolks and pepper.
A spaghetti dish made using such a sauce.
ety: From the Italian carbonara, shortening of alla carbonara (literally “in the manner of charcoal burners”, or “in the manner of the Carbonari”), ultimately from carbone (“coal”).

senses: A demonstration recording, often intended to show off the talent of an announcer to a prospective employer.
Synonym of winemaking.
ety: From vinify (“to make wine”) + -ication (suffix forming nouns).

senses: Patronizing behaviour or talk.
The region of outer space near Earth, including the upper atmosphere, ionosphere and magnetosphere.
The relationship of a godmother to the other godparents (godsibs or gossips), and the legal parents, of a child.
A female companion or intimate (of another woman).
Lass, the feminine equivalent of fellow.
ety: From Middle English commare, from Old French commere (modern French commère), from Late Latin commāter.

senses: A caption, title or other inscription, especially an Ancient Roman type.
ety: From Latin titulus. Doublet of tilde, titer/titre, title, titlo, and tittle.

senses: A dark brown pigment related to melanin
A baked dish of macaroni, ground beef, cheese and tomato sauce.
Ophiodon elongatus, a fish of the greenlings, of the family Hexagrammidae, native to the west coast of North America.
ety: From ling + cod, from its superficial resemblance to those two fish.

senses: Seeds or tissues maintained for the purpose of animal or plant breeding, preservation or other research uses.
ety: From germ + plasm. But compare germ plasm.

senses: The surface of a bench or workbench.
A kitchen counter.
A binturong (Arctictis binturong, in the family Viverridae).
Exhibiting or pertaining to misandry; hating or prejudiced against men.
A master of go.
Having camber.
The quality or state of being unknowable.
examples: At the end of her book we feel we know these couples as intimately as if we were part of their circle, but the ultimate nature of each relationship is left inviolate in its unknowability.

senses: Having one's personality in harmony or synergy with one's milieu.
Either of two New World vultures, Vultur gryphus of the Andes or Gymnogyps californianus, a nearly extinct vulture of the mountains of California.
A gold coin of some South American countries bearing the figure of one of these vultures.
An Argentinian short range ballistic missile.
ety: From Spanish cóndor, from Classical Quechua kuntur. The change /t/ to /d/ was characteristic of the "coastal" variety of the language.

senses: A measure of responsiveness.
One who writes down notes.
An electronic device for notetaking, typically used by the disabled.
examples: I went to sit down at the student computer. I have an electronic braille notetaker that is very much like a computer for me. It is a small portable device that has a braille keypad.

senses: A narrow-minded person or group that is overly concerned with censoring or criticizing personal conduct.
ety: Derived from Mrs. Grundy, a prudish character from the play Speed the Plough (1798) by the English playwright Thomas Morton.

senses: A type of primula, apparently originally from a hybrid between the cowslip and the primrose, having many different-coloured flowers.
ety: From Renaissance Latin polyanthus, corresponding to poly- + Ancient Greek ἄνθος (ánthos, “flower”).

senses: Any male ancestor.
Any of a number of methods of change-ringing on bells.
ety: From Middle English graunsire; compare grand and sire.

senses: A person who nurtures someone or something.
examples: Right then a ball is thwacked into Ari’s window leaving a spider web of cracks. Then the nurturer of grassroots street cricket runs out into the street, screaming, and confiscates the ball.

senses: Exhibiting photoluminescence
A fast food pastry, being a square doughnut with raisins and glaze.
A large cooking pot; a Dutch pot; a Dutch oven.
ety: From Dutch + -ie. It is unclear whether the sense of a cannabis joint comes from an earlier meaning of cannabis blunt rolled using a Dutch Masters cigar or whether it instead derives from the song Pass the Dutchie, which is itself based on the song Pass the Kouchie (where kouchie in the title refers to koutchie (a pipe for smoking cannabis)).

senses: A person who breeds or trains hawks or other birds of prey.
One who follows the sport of fowling with hawks.
ety: From Middle English fauconer, from Old French falconer, fauconer, from faucon (“falcon”).

senses: Having or showing a sharp or critical quality.
Serving to fix a dye to a fiber.
ety: From French mordant, from Latin mordeō. Doublet of mordent.

senses: Someone interested in, or owning a lot of, gadgets.
